newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply lower on late selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply lower on late selling.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Wednesday as the market's recent inability to break resistance opened a late floodgate of profit-taking, brokers said.
The weighted index held to a narrow range for most of the session, but dropped off in late trade to close 65.12 points or 0.98 percent lower at 6,551.26.
Turnover was an active T$58.68 billion.
The downturn registered across the board, but was felt worst in two recently robust sectors: textiles, which dropped 1.80 percent, and food shares, which lost 1.37 percent.

"The only way to explain the sudden selling is psychological fear with the index being unable to seek higher limits, because there really wasn't any other bearish factor to affect the market," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities.
The market had languished in a short-range consolidation since setting a 19-month high on October 5.
Hung cautioned that the market's recent sluggishness could prompt some investors to switch their holdings to far more bullish markets in Hong Kong and the United States.
Textile firm Hualon Corp dropped 3.83 percent or T$1.10 to T$27.60 in hectic trade involving 69.55 million shares.
Taiwan Tea Corp fell by 4.29 percent or T$3 to T$67.
Even the electronic sector lost 0.37 percent despite sound profit expectations and recent news that the U.S. semiconductor book-to-bill ratio reached a new year high in September.
"The market is relying too much on the electronics to spark a rally. But the fact is most semiconductor shares have already risen a lot and their upside is limited," Nikko's Hung said.

Brokers expect a near-term lack of clear direction as firms report mixed earning results for the first three quarters. The index was seen settling back into a consolidation on Thursday with an expected range of 6,530-6,600. -- Kevin Chen (5080815)
